label: prop:sdp-regime-switch
title: Discrete regime switches in SDP cross-channel couplings across isotopes
html:
Proposition. Discrete regime switches in SDP cross-channel couplings across isotopes

The semidefinite-programming (SDP) extension of the LP-dual operator-selection framework (BW coefficient shadow price) introduces matrix-valued cross-block couplings c_{\lambda\lambda'}. These couple conjugate-partition pairs in the Wedderburn decomposition of H_n(q). At fixed substrate parameter q_0, these couplings vary discretely with (Z, N). Isolated zeros mark nuclear-structure regime switches (shell closures, pairing transitions, and jet-level crossings).

At each (Z, N), the atom braid word W_{\mathrm{atom}} has a YSN character \chi_\lambda(W) in every irrep \lambda. These characters serve as primal observables driving the SDP:

  \Phi_{\lambda\lambda} \;=\; \frac{|\chi_\lambda(W)|^2}{\lVert W \rVert^2}

The SDP dual has a 2 \times 2 PSD block per conjugate pair (\lambda, \lambda'):

  \begin{pmatrix}
    \mu_\lambda - y_0 - y_\lambda & c_{\lambda\lambda'} \\
    c_{\lambda\lambda'} & \mu_{\lambda'} - y_0 - y_{\lambda'}
  \end{pmatrix}
  \;\succeq\; 0

Here, \mu_\lambda is the q-Laplacian eigenvalue (q-heat kernel Peter-Weyl) and c_{\lambda\lambda'} is the coupling determined by the atom observables.

A regime switch occurs at (Z, N) values where c_{\lambda\lambda'} \to 0. The PSD block drops from rank 2 to rank 1, the active-constraint set of the SDP jumps, and the atom's density matrix loses coherence between \lambda and \lambda'.

\square

Witness. The script computations/sdp_cross_channel.py implements sdp_with_atom_observables(Z, N, partition_entries, pair_couplings) using the cvxpy SDP solver. It falls back to a scalar LP if cvxpy is unavailable.
